sec: Mechanism-based classification and Group I hormones · p832

items.q: Match the Group I hormone feature — 1) Receptor  2) Solubility  3) Carrier protein  4) t½ … A) Lipophilic  B) Long  C) Intracellular (cytoplasm/nucleus)  D) Present (+)
items.exp: Group I: intracellular receptor, lipophilic, carrier protein (+), long t½; Group II is the opposite (cell membrane, hydrophilic, −, short). (Book p832)

items.q: Match the Group II hormone feature — 1) Receptor  2) Solubility  3) Carrier protein  4) t½ … A) Hydrophilic  B) Short  C) Cell membrane  D) Absent (−)
items.exp: Group II: cell-mbrane receptor, hydrophilic, no carrier protein, short t½. (Book p832)

items.q: Group I hormone actions are mediated through the receptor–hormone complex acting mainly on:
items.exp: Group I acts through gene transcription far more than transport channels. (Book p832)

items.q: Match receptor type to location/hormone — 1) Type I/homodimer  2) Type 2/heterodimer … A) Receptor in nucleus; T3, T4, vitamin A & D  B) Receptor in cytoplasm; steroid hormones
items.exp: Type I/homodimer receptors sit in the cytoplasm and bind steroid hormones; Type 2/heterodimer receptors sit in the nucleus and bind T3, T4, vitamin A & D. (Book p832)

items.q: In the Type I receptor, the chaperone that holds the receptor in an inactive form is ___.
items.exp: Hsp-90 is the chaperone keeping the steroid receptor inactive until hormone binds. (Book p832)

items.q: ‘When the steroid hormone binds, Hsp-90 dissociates and the receptor–hormone complex becomes active.’
items.exp: Hormone binding releases Hsp-90, forming the active R–H complex that enters the nucleus. (Book p832)

items.q: The active steroid receptor–hormone complex binds DNA at the:
items.exp: The complex binds glucocorticoid response elements (GRE) to drive gene transcription. (Book p832)
